title.en: State the role of an operating system
Explain process, memory, file and device management

say.en: You are playing music, downloading a file and typing notes at the same time. Who decides which program gets the CPU and memory? In this lesson: State the role of an operating system.
Describe types of user interface.
Explain process, memory, file and device management.

body.en: An *operating system* (OS) is system software that manages the computer's resources and provides an interface between the user and the hardware. Examples are Windows, Linux, macOS, Android and iOS. The OS offers a user interface: a command-line interface (CLI) where commands are typed, a graphical user interface (GUI) with windows, icons and menus, a touch interface on phones, and voice- or gesture-based interfaces.

points.en: Touch, voice and gesture interfaces on modern devices

title.en: On the board: Where the operating system sits

say.en: The operating system sits between the hardware and the applications the user runs.
The user talks to it through an interface: typed commands, windows and icons, touch, voice or gestures.
The OS manages four resources. Process management decides which program gets the CPU and for how long.
Memory management gives memory to each process and takes it back when the process ends.
File management creates, opens, copies and deletes files and folders.
Device management controls printers, disks and other devices through device drivers.

tagline.en: System software, programming tools and application software; machine, assembly and high-level languages; assembler, compiler and interpreter; open-source and proprietary software; functions of an operating system and its user interfaces.

myth.en: An interpreter checks the whole program first and then shows all the errors together.

truth.en: That is what a compiler does. An interpreter runs the program line by line and stops at the first line with an error; lines before it have already run. Both are translators, so they are easy to swap. Picture Python: a program that divides by zero on line 5 still prints the output of lines 1 to 4 before the error message.

say.en: The CPU understands only machine language: instructions written in 0s and 1s. It is fast but very hard for people to write.

problem.en: Name the OS function at work in each case: (a) a USB printer starts working after you plug it in (b) a closed app's memory becomes available to others (c) you move a file into a new folder.

steps.en: Controlling a newly attached device through its driver is device management: (a).
Freeing the memory of a closed program is memory management: (b).
Organising files and folders is file management: (c).

answer.en: (a) device management, (b) memory management, (c) file management
